title: Establishing the Premium Still to Be Collected on a Protection Plan
content:
The premium still to be collected on a Pass and Trip Protection plan is established from the plan's own record
and from the payments matched to premium entries on its protection account.

| The records show | The premium still to be collected |
| --- | --- |
| The premium frozen on the plan standing above the payments matched to premium entries on the protection account, and the balance the plan's record carries standing below the difference between them | The premium frozen on the plan less the payments matched to premium entries, rounded to the cent |
| The protection account carrying no payment matched to a premium entry | The whole premium frozen on the plan |
| Any other case | The balance the plan's own record carries |

**Reading the schedule.** The rows are read in the order given, and the first is compound: both of its limbs
must hold together — the premium frozen on the plan above the total of the payments matched to premium
entries, and the balance the plan's record carries below the difference between those two figures. Where the
first row's two limbs do not both hold, the second asks only whether the protection account carries any
payment matched to a premium entry at all.

**Worked cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan with a premium of 195.00 USD frozen on it, 60.00 USD of
payments matched to premium entries, and a balance of 90.00 USD on its record: the premium frozen stands above
the payments, and 90.00 USD stands below the difference of 135.00 USD, so the premium still to be collected is
135.00 USD. The same plan with a balance of 150.00 USD on its record: 150.00 USD does not stand below the
difference of 135.00 USD, and the account does carry a matched payment, so the premium still to be collected
is the 150.00 USD the record carries. A plan with a premium of 195.00 USD frozen on it and no payment at all
matched to a premium entry: the premium still to be collected is the whole 195.00 USD.
